notes: Only 2 of the 3 featured posts are from this run: no other Tier 1 research paper qualified, so MACH2 was kept as the third.

The SARS-CoV-2 and endometriosis papers are posted under the 'every purely computational Tier 1 paper' rule; the abstracts don't state explicitly that no new data were generated, so this is a judgement call.

Rules unclear: whether plant, microbial or viral papers that are purely computational in Tier 1 journals count (treated as out of scope); whether chordoma Letters with no abstract should override the Letter exclusion (skipped).
THREADS has no day in PubMed (2026 Nov), so its published date is blank and the added date is shown. Several Tier 2 papers were published in Sep-Oct but entered PubMed this week.

bioRxiv search_preprints returns 30 rows per call regardless of limit=100, so pages were read by 30 until a short page (about 424 rows across the four categories). Revised-version DOIs (v2/v3) never posted before were treated as new.

No tag exists for DNA damage or mutational signatures; Epigenomics and Clinical were used as closest tags. No reusable-license Figure 1 was confirmed for the featured journal papers, so illustrations were drawn.

notes: README says to page bioRxiv until a page returns fewer than 100 results, but the connector returns about 30 per page whatever the limit; I paged until a page came back empty instead (1 to 8 pages per category).

The four bioRxiv category scans were done by helper agents that read titles and 200-character previews, so 'purely computational' calls for preprints are partly judged from the preview; abstracts were read in full for all posted preprints.

PubMed 'get_article_metadata' returns at most 20 papers per call; several Tier 2 hits have an older publication date (Aug-Oct) but a PubMed entry date inside the 7-day window, so they were treated as new.
No PubMed licence allowed figure reuse (none CC BY), so all three featured pictures are hand-drawn illustrations.
Unclear rule: whether Nature Methods-style 'Review' articles in research journals (Nat Genet, Nat Methods, Mol Cell) count as reviews; I skipped them since only the four review journals qualify.
Tier 2 and preprint tabs both hit the 10-paper limit, so several on-topic papers were left out.

notes: The bioRxiv connector returns at most 30 results per page even with limit=100, so pages were read in steps of 30 until a short or empty page; bioinformatics ran to 7 pages, genomics 3, cancer biology 4 and genetics 2.

For several revised preprints (v2 or later) get_preprint returns the v1 record, so the abstract may differ from the current version. ModkitOpt is listed as v5 but first posted in December 2025; it was treated as new because its DOI had never been posted, and its posted date is the listing date.
The Genome Medicine lung-to-tumour eQTL paper has an August 2026 online date but entered PubMed in the 7-day window, so it was posted on its PubMed entry date.

The README says to page until fewer than 100 results, which does not fit the 30-per-page connector limit; the screening of the four bioRxiv categories was done in parallel by subagents and the bioinformatics category was read by hand after one subagent returned without screening.
Chordoma screening of bioRxiv used titles and abstract previews, so a chordoma mention deeper in an abstract would not have been seen.

notes: Scan sizes: PubMed search 1 returned 132 results, search 2 92, search 3 33, search 4 34, search 5 31 (48 unique across 4 and 5), search 6 5, search 7 4; all were read. bioRxiv: bioinformatics about 200 listings, genomics 77, cancer biology 53, genetics 26.

Searches 4 and 5: the * wildcard was again replaced by explicit forms. The low counts look real: the same four journals with only hasabstract gave 390 entries for the window, so the keyword searches match under a tenth of them.
Chordoma: all 4 PubMed results were already posted, and no chordoma preprint appeared in the four bioRxiv categories.

bioRxiv connector: pages are capped at 30 whatever the limit, so scans paged until an empty page. It gave many 30-second timeouts and 503s; the 7-day genetics and bioinformatics queries had to be split into shorter date ranges, and one shortlisted preprint (human 5S rDNA array methylation) could never be fetched and was dropped. The cancer biology count (53) still looks low for a week.

get_preprint returns the first version for revised preprints. Four posted preprints (HIDE-Deconv v3, the t-test reformulation v2, the single-cell foundation model benchmark v2, HGSC subtypes v2) use the new listing title and date with a summary based on the v1 abstract; each summary says so.
get_copyright_status returned no licence for the three featured papers, so all three got hand-drawn illustrations.

Unclear rule: the Canine Cancer Genome Atlas (Science) is veterinary genomics, which is listed as out of scope, but it is cancer genomics with a direct human comparison, so it was posted and featured. PubMed strips the gene names from its abstract, so the summary and illustration name no drivers. It is tagged Computational although the abstract does not say whether any sequencing was new.

Unclear rule: Cell published the BICAN basal ganglia package (about 17 brain atlas papers). Three were posted as Methods, following earlier single-cell atlas posts; say if all or none of the package is wanted.
BRCA1 saturation genome editing (Nat Genet) is germline variant interpretation rather than tumour genomics; it was posted last in Tier 1 as a borderline case.

Preprints were ranked by approach first, as the rules say, so all ten posted are purely computational and several closely matching mixed or experimental preprints were left out; they can still be picked on a later run.

No tags exist for pangenomes, cell-free DNA/liquid biopsy, CRISPR and variant-effect screens, TWAS/eQTL, circRNA or translation; those aspects were left untagged. TransCirc 2.0 carries RNA modifications only because m6A is one of its evidence layers.
Some PubMed publication dates are earlier than the entry date; the published field uses the PubMed date as given.

notes: PubMed searches 4 and 5 (broad journals): the tool rejects the * wildcard, so isoform*, benchmark*, genomic*, transcriptom* and epigenom* were replaced by explicit forms (isoform OR isoforms, etc.), which pushes search 4 over 20 operators as counted in the config; PubMed accepted it. Each search returned only 36 results, which is low for these four journals.

The screen of searches 4 and 5 was stopped by an automated model safeguard just as it finished reporting. Counts and four complete candidates had already been delivered and were used; a fifth (SCRAMseq) and the near-miss list were lost. The screen was not re-run.

bioRxiv connector: search_preprints returns at most 30 results per page even with limit=100, so the README rule 'stop when a page has fewer than 100' would stop after the first page. Scans paged by 30 until an empty page: bioinformatics 218 listings, genomics 80, cancer biology 37, genetics 23. The cancer biology and genetics totals look low and the connector gave repeated timeouts and 503s, so some preprints may have been missed.

get_preprint returns the first version's record for revised preprints. Four posted preprints (AbSplice development, SpacePhenotyper, RICO, simple models vs foundation models) use the new version's title and date from the listing with a summary based on the v1 abstract; each summary says so.
get_copyright_status returned no licence for the featured papers, so all three got hand-drawn illustrations instead of Figure 1.

Unclear rule: 'post every purely computational biology paper' in Tier 1 versus plant/ecological work being out of scope. The Nature cactus extinction-risk modelling paper was skipped; say if such papers should be posted.

Some PubMed records for Genome Biology, Genome Medicine and Nature Communications papers carry August or October publication dates despite entering PubMed this week; the 'published' field uses PubMed's date as given.
No tag exists for population genetics/eQTL mapping (jaxQTL) or liquid biopsy (breast epigenetics paper); those aspects were left untagged.
